Let the six vertices of the octahedron be represented by  
\(\pm x,\pm y,\pm z\). A face contains three mutually adjacent vertices, and the face across an edge replaces the third vertex by its opposite.

### 1. Fold the net

Assign the three vertices of face \(3\) as \(+x,+y,+z\). Propagating this assignment across the net gives:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Face}&\text{Folded vertices}\\ \hline
1&(+x,+y,-z)\\
2&(-x,+y,+z)\\
3&(+x,+y,+z)\\
4&(+x,-y,+z)\\
5&(-x,-y,+z)\\
6&(-x,-y,-z)\\
7&(+x,-y,-z)\\
Q&(-x,+y,-z)
\end{array}
\]

Thus the three edges of \(Q\) are:

- \((-x,-z)\), shared with face \(6\);
- \((-x,+y)\), shared with face \(2\);
- \((+y,-z)\), shared with face \(1\).

### 2. Identify the edge on the right

In the net, the vertices of \(Q\) are arranged as

\[
\begin{array}{c}
-z\\[-2mm]
(-x)\qquad(+y)
\end{array}
\]

In the completed octahedron, the printed \(Q\) is upright in the upper-left face, so its upper-right edge is the edge joining \(-z\) to \(+y\). The face on the other side of this edge is face \(1\).

Therefore, the numbered face to the right of \(Q\) is

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
